text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Government seeks to privatise in 1997 the new unit formed by a merger between aircraft manufacturers Dassault and state-owned Aerospatiale announced by the finance ministry on Tuesday. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Lazard investment bank chairman Michel David-Weill in an interview says his successor has not yet been chosen, sees space for independent investment banks in France.
-- Employment and costs monitoring body CSERC calls for increased labour flexibility within firms rather than on an open work market, as it tends to increase income inequality.
-- New Aerospatiale Dassault unit once privatised may bid for defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, and could consider an alliance with Alcatel.
-- PSA carmaker and L'Oreal cosmetics group chosen by the newspaper in a contest of firms which enhance research and development.

-- EU authorities to be presented with state bailout project for Credit Lyonnais, to check whether it complies with antitrust rules, while bank chairman Jean Peyrelevade calls for further state help ahead of a privatisation.
-- SBF bourse association seeks to increase by 10 percent the number of listed companies in 1997.
-- Part-time work may have helped to save up to 400,000 jobs from 1990 to 1995, study shows, as France lost less jobs than its European neighbours.
-- Forecasts see German growth around 2 percent in 1997, not enough to meet the Maastricht treaty criteria on public deficits.
-- European parliament report says EU Commission in the management of the BSE "mad cow" crisis leaned toward supporting the meat industry rather than public health.
-- Former chief of security at the French presidency allegedly took part in recruiting several hundred European and African mercenaries assembling in eastern Zaire to fight rebels.
-- Canal Plus reaches agreement with PolyGram on broadcast rights.
